# H2-Receptor Antagonists vs. Proton Pump Inhibitors for GERD

Based on the available evidence, both options are used for GERD, but the retrieved sources provide limited direct comparison of when each is most appropriate.

## Proton Pump Inhibitors

PPIs (dexlansoprazole, esomeprazole, lansoprazole, omeprazole, pantoprazole magnesium, pantoprazole sodium, and rabeprazole) work by irreversibly binding to and inhibiting the hydrogen-potassium ATPase on the parietal cell membrane, effectively blocking acid secretion [Source 1: gastroesophageal_reflux_disease.md].

At equivalent doses, available PPIs offer similar symptom relief, tolerability, and safety; cost is the major factor in choosing between them [Source 1: gastroesophageal_reflux_disease.md].

## H2-Receptor Antagonists

H2RAs (cimetidine, famotidine, nizatidine, and ranitidine) reduce gastric acid by blocking histamine receptors, which reversibly inhibit the action of the proton pump and prevent the movement of hydrogen ions into the stomach. All H2RAs are considered equally effective and have an excellent safety profile [Source 2: dyspepsia_gerd.pdf]. The relief of GERD symptoms with H2RAs appears similar to antacids but with longer duration of effect [Source 2: dyspepsia_gerd.pdf].

## Important Drug Interaction Note

**Cimetidine** decreases cytochrome P450 metabolism of other drugs (e.g., phenytoin, theophylline, warfarin), whereas other H2RAs (famotidine and nizatidine) have minimal effects [Source 5: dyspepsia_and_peptic_ulcer_disease.md]. For your patient, **famotidine** would be preferable to cimetidine if an H2RA is chosen.
